title: AP-Free Sets
content: Defines `APFree A` for $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$: no three elements $a, a+d, a+2d$ with $d \ne 0$ all belong to $A$. Working in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ (cyclic group) rather than $[N]$ simplifies the Fourier analysis since the Pontryagin dual is $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ itself. The condition $d \ne 0$ excludes degenerate constant progressions.
mathContext: $A \text{ is AP-free} \iff \forall a, d \in \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z},\; d \ne 0 \implies \neg(a \in A \land a+d \in A \land a+2d \in A)$

title: Base Cases: Empty and Singleton
content: Proves that the empty set and singletons are AP-free. For the empty set, no element belongs to $\emptyset$. For singletons $\{x\}$, if $a = x$ and $a + d = x$, then $d = 0$, contradicting $d \ne 0$. These base cases anchor the inductive density argument: the iteration must terminate because density cannot exceed 1 on any subprogression.

title: Fourier Coefficients
content: Defines the Fourier coefficient $\hat{1}_A(r) = \sum_{x \in A} e^{2\pi i r x / N}$ using complex exponentials. This is the discrete Fourier transform of the characteristic function $1_A$ on $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$. The key property (proved in `fourier_large_coefficient`) is that AP-free sets must have a large non-trivial Fourier coefficient, revealing hidden additive structure.

title: Large Fourier Coefficient from AP-Free Density
content: States the key analytic step: if $A$ has density $\delta$ and no 3-AP, then there exists a non-trivial frequency $r \ne 0$ with $|\hat{1}_A(r)| \ge \delta^2 N / 2$. The proof would use the 3-AP counting formula $\Lambda_3(A) = N^{-1} \sum_r |\hat{1}_A(r)|^2 \hat{1}_A(-2r)$. If $\Lambda_3 = 0$ (no 3-APs) and $|\hat{1}_A(0)| = |A| = \delta N$, then by Parseval some non-trivial coefficient must be large to absorb the $\delta^3 N^2$ contribution from $r = 0$.

title: Density Increment Lemma
content: States the core inductive step: if $A$ has density $\delta$ and no 3-AP in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$, then there exists a subprogression of length $\ge \sqrt{N}$ where $A$ has density $\ge \delta + \delta^2/100$. The proof would convert a large Fourier coefficient into a density increment on an arithmetic subprogression using a standard argument: the large coefficient witnesses correlation with a character, which localizes density to a coset. The increment $\delta^2/100$ ensures termination after $O(1/\delta)$ steps.

title: Roth's Theorem: r₃(N) = o(N)
content: States the main result: for every $\delta > 0$, every sufficiently large AP-free subset of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ has density less than $\delta$. The proof would iterate `density_increment_lemma`: starting with density $\delta$, each step increases density by $\delta^2/100$ on a subprogression of length $\ge \sqrt{N}$. After $\lceil 100/\delta \rceil$ steps, the density exceeds 1, which is impossible, so the set cannot be AP-free. The subprogression length decreases by square roots, requiring $N$ to be at least a tower of exponentials in $1/\delta$.
mathContext: $\forall \delta > 0,\; \exists N_0 : N \ge N_0 \implies |A| \ge \delta N \implies A \text{ contains a 3-AP}$
